negative_findings.description: Targeted searching for Bank360.hu A5 content (leadership moves, appointments) returned no matching articles from that domain; results were dominated by Portfolio, Privátbankár and Növekedés instead.
negative_findings.result_summary: Bank360.hu appears to be primarily a product-comparison portal rather than a personnel-news outlet; retained as low-priority candidate, not confirmed as an A5 channel.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Prevents the collection pipeline from spending a scheduled poller on a channel with near-zero A5 recall.

negative_findings.description: Attempted fetch of https://privatbankar.hu/cikkek/karrier returned HTTP 404; the correct section path is https://privatbankar.hu/cikkek/karrier.html (with .html suffix), confirmed via search result titles.
negative_findings.result_summary: Not a dead source — a path-convention issue. Privátbankár uses .html-suffixed section and tag URLs.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A naive crawler using extension-less section paths would mark this high-value karrier column as dead.

negative_findings.description: An English-syntax query combining index.hu/telex.hu with 'bank vezérigazgató kinevezés 2026' returned mostly irrelevant EU-document PDFs; the same outlets surfaced correctly only when reached via hu-language snowballing from other queries.
negative_findings.result_summary: Site-scoped queries against Hungarian general-news domains are unreliable through this search interface; section crawling / RSS is the dependable route.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Discovery strategy for Index and Telex must be crawl-based, not search-based, or coverage will be silently incomplete.

negative_findings.description: Per-section RSS endpoints were only inferred from the Portfolio RSS index page description; individual feed URLs (e.g. a bank-section XML) were not independently confirmed in this pass, and RSS availability for Privátbankár, vg.hu, Növekedés, HRPWR, FinTechRadar and FinTechZone was not established.
negative_findings.result_summary: Feed-level access is a hypothesis pending the deterministic verification pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection method choice (RSS poller vs HTML crawler) per source is still open for most of the cell.

negative_findings.description: Portfolio.hu and HVG.hu both operate partial subscription models (Portfolio Signature / hvg360); some in-depth leadership and restructuring pieces are likely subscriber-only. Extent not measured in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: Headline-level A5 signal appears to remain free; detail may be gated.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Affects whether entity-level extraction (names, dates, remits) is possible without a paid subscription.

coverage_gaps.description: No wire-service source identified in this cell. MTI/OS (Országos Sajtószolgálat) is the upstream that many of these outlets republish verbatim; adding it would give earlier, deduplicated, structurally uniform appointment items.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Scout os.mti.hu / mti.hu press-release feeds for banking-sector personnel announcements and treat as a direct/pointer source upstream of this press cell.

coverage_gaps.description: Cell coverage is heavily skewed to C-suite and deputy-CEO appointments. Ordinary hiring signals (open vacancies, headcount growth, new team builds in payments/cards/IT) are not covered by the press channel at all.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Ensure another cell owns job boards (profession.hu, cvonline.hu, LinkedIn Jobs) and bank careers pages; press should not be relied on for 'jobs'/'hiring' recall.

coverage_gaps.description: Payments-specific actors (card schemes, acquirers, PSPs, ATM/POS vendors, GIRO/Takarékinfo-type infrastructure) are far less covered by these general business outlets than banks are; discovered examples were almost entirely bank-side.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add payments trade and vendor-side channels (e.g. GIRO Zrt. communications, Mastercard/Visa Hungary press, payments-specific trade press) and test A5 yield.

coverage_gaps.description: Only one en-language Hungary-focused outlet (BBJ) was captured; other English channels (Hungary Today, Daily News Hungary, Telex English, Reuters/Bloomberg Hungary coverage) were not scouted in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a second en-language sweep for Hungary-focused English business press with appointments coverage.

coverage_gaps.description: No archival/backfill strategy established. Executive career-path history (who moved from OTP to MBH, when) requires multi-year archive access; mfor.hu and HR Portál tag pages look like the best backfill assets but pagination depth is unknown.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Test deep pagination on mfor.hu site search and hrportal.hu tag indices; consider archive.org for outlets that truncate.

coverage_gaps.description: Robots.txt / terms-of-service posture for automated collection was not inspected for any domain in this cell.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Have the deterministic pass fetch robots.txt and ToS for all listed domains before enabling crawlers; prefer publisher RSS where offered.

brief: Hungarian-language business press is a dense, high-recall channel for A5 signals, anchored by Portfolio.hu's Bank section (with publisher RSS), Privátbankár's dedicated Karrier/karrierhír column, and vg.hu for state-owned financial institutions where appointments are politically driven. Telex and HVG supply the counter-signal that corporate sources never publish — layoffs, post-merger restructuring and forced exits — while Forbes.hu and FinTechRadar/FinTechZone are the only reliable routes to fintech and neobank leadership. BBJ's English 'Appointments' column is the most structured single feed in the cell and is the natural machine-readable spine, with mfor.hu and ProfitLine acting as archive depth and redundancy respectively. Main weaknesses: the press channel covers executives but not ordinary hiring, under-covers payments infrastructure versus banks, and lacks the upstream MTI/OS wire that several of these outlets simply republish.
